quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: An invitation has two parts: a question and the reason for it.
quests.explanation: Text and speech are identical. Asking "are you free" before making an invitation is a friendly way to check if someone can come.
quests.prompt: Are you free on Saturday? We're having a barbecue.
quests.sampleAnswer: Are you free on Saturday? We're having a barbecue.
quests.followUpQuestion: Invite a friend to something this weekend.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A polite refusal has a positive start, then a turn. Listen for the turn.
quests.explanation: You heard exactly what was written. "I'd love to, but" softens a refusal, and the real reason comes after "but".
quests.prompt: I'd love to come, but I have to work.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'd love to come, but I have to work.
quests.followUpQuestion: How would you turn down an invitation politely?

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A suggestion is made with "Why don't we". What is the place near?
quests.explanation: Office and house give different meeting spots. The suggestion sounds friendly either way, but you would travel somewhere else.
quests.prompt: Why don't we meet at the cafe near your office?
quests.sampleAnswer: Why don't we meet at the cafe near your house?
quests.followUpQuestion: Suggest a place to meet a friend.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: An apology with an excuse. Follow the excuse to the end.
quests.explanation: A perfect match. Using "terrible" instead of "bad" makes the excuse sound more dramatic.
quests.prompt: Sorry I'm late, the traffic was terrible this morning.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sorry I'm late, the traffic was terrible this morning.
quests.followUpQuestion: Give a short excuse for being late.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A very polite request. The direction word is small but powerful.
quests.explanation: Down and up ask for opposite things. A neighbour who hears the wrong one could make the noise worse.
quests.prompt: Would you mind turning the music down a little?
quests.sampleAnswer: Would you mind turning the music up a little?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask someone politely to be quieter.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two jobs are shared out. Who does which?
quests.explanation: Every word is the same but the responsibilities are swapped. At a party, this is how you end up with no drinks.
quests.prompt: I'll bring the drinks if you can get the snacks.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'll bring the snacks if you can get the drinks.
quests.followUpQuestion: Share out jobs for a party with a friend.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A reaction and a preference. The second half decides.
quests.explanation: "I'd rather" means "I would prefer to", and it is followed by the bare verb.
quests.prompt: That sounds great, but I'd rather stay in tonight.
quests.sampleAnswer: That sounds great, but I'd rather stay in tonight.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you'd rather do this evening.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A reassurance with a negative near the end.
quests.explanation: The speech follows the text. "It wasn't your fault" is a kind way to stop someone from feeling guilty.
quests.prompt: Don't worry about it, it really wasn't your fault.
quests.sampleAnswer: Don't worry about it, it really wasn't your fault.
quests.followUpQuestion: Comfort a friend who made a small mistake.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The preference comes first. A phrase at the end says when.
quests.explanation: Afternoon and morning are opposite ends of the day, and this speaker's habit turns out to be different.
quests.prompt: I prefer tea to coffee, especially in the afternoon.
quests.sampleAnswer: I prefer tea to coffee, especially in the morning.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say your favourite drink and the time you have it.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A thank-you starts the sentence. Listen to the pronoun after "inviting".
quests.explanation: Me is one guest and us is the speaker plus others. Thanking a host for a whole group is not the same as thanking them for one person.
quests.prompt: Thanks for inviting me, I had a wonderful evening.
quests.sampleAnswer: Thanks for inviting us, I had a wonderful evening.
quests.followUpQuestion: Thank a host as you leave a party.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Agreement and disagreement in the same short sentence.
quests.explanation: "But only partly" shows a careful, polite way to say you don't fully agree.
quests.prompt: I agree with you, but only partly.
quests.sampleAnswer: I agree with you, but only partly.
quests.followUpQuestion: Partly agree with an idea, in your own words.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two people appear in this request. Work out who calls whom.
quests.explanation: The words are nearly identical, but the reminder is for a different person and the call goes in another direction.
quests.prompt: Could you remind me to call Mum tomorrow?
quests.sampleAnswer: Could you remind Mum to call me tomorrow?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask someone to remind you about something.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The event is the important noun at the end.
quests.explanation: A wedding and a party are different kinds of event, and missing a wedding would be much more serious.
quests.prompt: I'm afraid I can't make it to your wedding.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm afraid I can't make it to your party.
quests.followUpQuestion: Apologise because you can't come to something.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Reassurance often comes in a short pair of phrases.
quests.explanation: Nothing was altered in this one. "As long as you need" gives the other person all the time they want.
quests.prompt: No problem at all, take as long as you need.
quests.sampleAnswer: No problem at all, take as long as you need.
quests.followUpQuestion: Tell someone they don't need to hurry.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: This idiom is a friendly way to suggest meeting. Catch it at the start.
quests.explanation: "Catch up" means to share news after a long time, and "ages" is an informal way to say a long time.
quests.prompt: We should catch up soon, it's been ages since we talked.
quests.sampleAnswer: We should catch up soon, it's been ages since we talked.
quests.followUpQuestion: How would you suggest catching up with an old friend?

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A relaxed invitation begins with a condition.
quests.explanation: The text and audio are alike. "Come round" is a common British way to say visit my place.
quests.prompt: If you're not busy, come round and watch the match.
quests.sampleAnswer: If you're not busy, come round and watch the match.
quests.followUpQuestion: Invite someone over to watch something.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The apology names something the speaker regrets. Find the verb.
quests.explanation: Upsetting someone is emotional, and interrupting is about conversation. The second half, "please carry on", makes sense with only one.
quests.prompt: I didn't mean to upset you, please carry on.
quests.sampleAnswer: I didn't mean to interrupt you, please carry on.
quests.followUpQuestion: Apologise for interrupting someone.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A recommendation includes a word that shows how certain it is.
quests.explanation: Definitely is much stronger than probably. Listeners might decide differently about going out because of that one word.
quests.prompt: My friend says the new restaurant is definitely worth trying.
quests.sampleAnswer: My friend says the new restaurant is probably worth trying.
quests.followUpQuestion: Recommend a place you like, and say how sure you are.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two offers appear in one sentence, split by "and".
quests.explanation: They agree. Offering to buy the next round is a friendly way to be fair at the end of the evening.
quests.prompt: Let's split the bill, and I'll get the next round.
quests.sampleAnswer: Let's split the bill, and I'll get the next round.
quests.followUpQuestion: How would you offer to pay next time?

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The message is about timing. Which event does the text depend on?
quests.explanation: Getting there and leaving are opposite ends of a trip. The person waiting at home would get the message at the wrong time.
quests.prompt: I'll text you when I get there, don't wait up.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'll text you when I leave, don't wait up.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say when you will send someone a message.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A host is speaking. Listen to the negative and to what comes after the comma.
quests.explanation: It's what you read. "Just yourself" is a warm way to say that nothing else is necessary.
quests.prompt: You don't have to bring anything, just yourself.
quests.sampleAnswer: You don't have to bring anything, just yourself.
quests.followUpQuestion: What would you say to a guest who asks what to bring?

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: An opening word softens a request. What comes after it?
quests.explanation: Same in both forms. "Actually" introduces a correction or a slight change of plan without sounding rude.
quests.prompt: Actually, I'd prefer to sit outside if that's okay.
quests.sampleAnswer: Actually, I'd prefer to sit outside if that's okay.
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask if you can change your seat.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two ways of saying thanks appear back to back.
quests.explanation: Adding "a lot" and "really" makes a thank-you feel warmer.
quests.prompt: Thanks a lot, I really appreciate your help with this.
quests.sampleAnswer: Thanks a lot, I really appreciate your help with this.
quests.followUpQuestion: Thank someone who helped you today.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A short word after "if" shows who is going to act.
quests.explanation: I and we mean one person or a group. In a shared room, the choice changes who is asking.
quests.prompt: Do you mind if I open the window?
quests.sampleAnswer: Do you mind if we open the window?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask permission to do something in a shared room.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The story has a person who promised something. Who is it?
quests.explanation: Both pronouns changed, and they refer to a different person. In conversation, mixing them up sends you to complain to the wrong friend.
quests.prompt: She said she'd call back, but she never did.
quests.sampleAnswer: He said he'd call back, but he never did.
quests.followUpQuestion: Tell a short story about someone who forgot to call.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two options for a plan. Keep them in order.
quests.explanation: Matching. "Would ... work for you" is a polite way to propose a day.
quests.prompt: Would Friday work for you, or is Saturday better?
quests.sampleAnswer: Would Friday work for you, or is Saturday better?
quests.followUpQuestion: Offer two days for a meeting and ask which is better.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The plan is about a place at the end of the first half.
quests.explanation: Coast and mountains lead to different weekends, one with beaches and the other with hills.
quests.prompt: We're thinking of going to the mountains for the weekend.
quests.sampleAnswer: We're thinking of going to the coast for the weekend.
quests.followUpQuestion: Talk about a plan you have for the weekend.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The invitation ends with a pronoun. Is it a group or one person?
quests.explanation: Us means the speaker plus others, and me means only the speaker. It changes how many people the guest will meet.
quests.prompt: I wasn't sure if you'd want to join us.
quests.sampleAnswer: I wasn't sure if you'd want to join me.
quests.followUpQuestion: Invite someone to join a group.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A polite question with an object left behind.
quests.explanation: Umbrella and phone are both things people forget on trains, but the owner would react differently to each one.
quests.prompt: Sorry to bother you, but is this your umbrella?
quests.sampleAnswer: Sorry to bother you, but is this your phone?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask a stranger if something belongs to them.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A warm farewell. Listen for how the speaker expresses a long gap.
quests.explanation: The recording follows the text word for word. "After all this time" is a very natural way to show you haven't met for years.
quests.prompt: It was so nice to see you again after all this time.
quests.sampleAnswer: It was so nice to see you again after all this time.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say goodbye to someone you haven't seen for years.
